messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED: us-east-1a egress/NAT flap affecting inference-serving pool (1798765432)
incident-bot: Severity: P1 — visible customer errors & elevated latency. Pager duty: @oncall-raj
oncall-raj: seeing spikes in 502/504s from a subset of inference endpoints in us-east-1a. Grafana dashboard: tail latency jump ~3x starting 12:08 UTC. Routing shows heavy retry churn.
sre-lina: confirmed. 502s concentrated on target group redwood-inf-us-east-1a-rtg. Health checks flapping for model fetch (S3) and auth metadata calls.
runtime-elaine: symptoms: kernels timing out on shard load (timeout to model registry), KV cache write errors. Service logs show outbound connection timeouts to 3rd-party tokenization endpoint and S3 endpoint in same AZ.
ops-jordan: network errors look like egress NAT gateway rate/connection problems in us-east-1a. AWS console shows NAT gateway metrics spike in active connections and SNAT exhaustion? Need AWS confirmation.
eng-ryan: impact measured: ~12% of all inference requests in region saw >=500ms and ~3% returned 502/504. Affected customers: 3 enterprise tenants (IDs redacted) on dedicated pools pinned to us-east-1a. Hosted customers degrade gracefully to lower throughput.
support-maya: we've started opening SEV tickets with the three customers; they are seeing errors and asking for ETA. We need ETA and mitigation plan.
oncall-raj: immediate mitigation options: 1) shift traffic away from us-east-1a (preferable), 2) create temporary egress path (add NAT in different subnet), 3) ask AWS to failover AZ resources (long). Which can we do fastest?
sre-lina: we can adjust routing at the service level — update smart routing policy to prefer us-east-1b/c for new requests and drain us-east-1a targets. Will be faster than DNS changes.
runtime-elaine: doing a canary move: 10% traffic to us-east-1b now. Watchers: latency, error rate, cache fill time.
eng-ryan: +1. push config change: 
```json
{ "smart_routing": { "region_preference": "us-east-1", "az_weights": { "us-east-1a": 0.05, "us-east-1b": 0.6, "us-east-1c": 0.35 } } }
```
ops-jordan: rolling that now via control plane. Updating 6 routes.
ops-jordan: update complete. Traffic shift in progress — monitoring.
sre-lina: after shift: error rate for requests originally hitting us-east-1a decreased from 3%->0.4% within 90s. Tail latency for moved requests stable.
support-maya: relaying to customers: we have shifted traffic to reduce impact, still investigating root cause. ETA: ongoing; will update in 15m.
eng-ryan: note: two dedicated customer pools pinned to us-east-1a are still experiencing issues because instances can't reach auth/token service in same AZ for some control-plane ops. They need full migration or manual reroute.
oncall-raj: starting manual migration for dedicated pools: spin up replacement nodes in us-east-1b and attach. Will do sequential to avoid cold-start storm.
runtime-elaine: command to add nodes (example):
```
# create replacement instances in us-east-1b and attach to pool
redwoodctl infra create-node --pool dedicated-cust-42 --az us-east-1b --instance-type g5.xlarge
redwoodctl infra attach-node --pool dedicated-cust-42 --node <id>
```
sre-lina: AWS Support opened case 1234567891; they are investigating NAT gateway capacity in us-east-1a and looking for other customer reports. Estimated AWS update in 30-45m.
ops-jordan: risk: DNS won't help quick because TTL is 60s but Route53 health checks also need time. Our control-plane routing change was fastest.
eng-ryan: monitoring shows CPU and GPU usage normal on moved nodes, but KV cache warm-up adds ~120ms P95 for initial requests — acceptable.
acct-carlos: impacted customer C is in contract with SLA. Need a temporary credit + communication. Support, can you draft message?
support-maya: on it. Draft to legal and account sent.
incident-bot: NOTE — next on-call handoff scheduled at 13:00 UTC, assign to @sre-lina for continued mitigation.
oncall-raj: handing off — summary: NAT gateway SNAT exhaustion suspected in us-east-1a causing outbound egress failures; we've shifted traffic away at service routing layer, manual migration in progress for dedicated pools, AWS support engaged. Attaching checklist.
sre-lina: taking over. Checklist items: 1) continue draining us-east-1a targets; 2) finish dedicated pool migrations (cust-42, cust-77); 3) confirm AWS remediation; 4) run post-incident telemetry collection.
runtime-elaine: help needed: we should lower autoscaler aggressiveness temporarily to avoid spinning up new nodes pinned to us-east-1a. Setting scale policy min-az to exclude 1a.
ops-jordan: applied: autoscaler policy updated to prefer 1b/1c. Command: 
```
redwoodctl autoscale update --policy global --exclude-az us-east-1a
```
sre-lina: AWS update: they confirmed a partial NAT gateway SNAT table exhaustion due to a noisy tenant with high ephemeral connections. They are throttling and recommending moving clients to other AZs; AWS will propose mitigation steps within 1h.
eng-ryan: metric snapshot pre-mitigation: us-east-1a active connections 23k (baseline 3k), NAT errors 1.8k/min, backend 502s up 320/min. Post-routing action: errors down to 40/min overall.
support-maya: customer comms: sent interim message to customers with mitigation steps and ask for logs. All acknowledged.
sre-lina: current status: incident mitigated for hosted customers; two dedicated pools 50% migrated (cust-42 done, cust-77 1 node left). No data loss. Severity staying P1 until AWS confirms fix.
incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: runbook steps and debug artifacts collected. Create postmortem draft in #postmortems and tag eng-runtime and eng-infra.
acct-carlos: please include timeline and list of customers impacted for billing review.
sre-lina: taking note. Estimated time to close: once AWS confirms NAT capacity restored and we finish dedicated migrations + postmortem.
oncall-raj: final note before handoff: reduce alerts to warnings for us-east-1a 502s once we see <50/min sustained for 15m.
sre-lina: ack. Moving to monitoring-only until AWS final confirmation. Will escalate if errors spike.
eng-ryan: post-incident items: 1) implement SNAT pooling + connection reuse in our egress clients, 2) add per-AZ traffic caps to autoscaler to avoid concentration, 3) create playbook for rapid cross-AZ migration for dedicated pools.
support-maya: will coordinate customer follow-ups and SLA credits.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity -> P2 (mitigated) at 1798765600.
sre-lina: closing loop: AWS case updated; they will clean up noisy tenant and increase SNAT capacity; we'll validate tomorrow morning. Postmortem owners: @eng-ryan (root cause & infra changes), @runtime-elaine (runtime mitigations).
oncall-raj: handing off fully to @sre-lina. Logging handoff message and start time 13:00 UTC.
sre-lina: thanks — I'll publish interim incident summary in 10m and create postmortem ticket.
support-maya: customers notified of mitigation and next steps.
acct-carlos: thanks everyone. Keep me posted before final closure so we can handle billing.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: 1798765650 (mitigated, postmortem required)
